Need the patient's skin biopsy histopathology report and Doppler ultrasound of the right shoulder lesion, as these are core examinations for distinguishing linear morphea/scleroderma from malignant infiltration or a low-flow vascular lesion, especially given the atypical arborizing purple papules and easy bruising.

Need the results of autoimmune serology (ANA, anti-Scl-70) and additional immunohistochemical stains (S100, CD1a, factor XIIIa) to exclude Langerhans cell histiocytosis and confirm the histiocytic infiltrate is intralymphatic, as these are essential to validate the leading hypothesis.

bindings.label: Irregularly linear, rusty-brown, atrophic, streaklike plaque extending from right shoulder to right biceps
The plaque ended in an arborizing purple plaque with scattered, slightly indurated, irregular papules within it; no warmth, thrills, or pulsations across the affected area.

Patient is a man in his 80s with an 18-month history of skin changes and mild tingling sensation within the lesion; he denied any triggers, causes, aggravating or alleviating factors, and had not attempted any treatments.

Review of systems was negative except easy bruising; current medications include finasteride, montelukast, enalapril, and metoprolol; medical history significant for right total reverse shoulder replacement 5 years prior.
Apart from the described lesion, physical examination was unremarkable, with full range of motion of the right shoulder.
Biopsy shows dense CD68+ histiocytic infiltrate in dermis and lymphatic vessels
D2-40 staining highlights lymphatic vessels with nodular clefting
Biopsy lacks sclerotic collagen pattern characteristic of morphea
Autoimmune serology and S100, CD1a, factor XIIIa immunohistochemistry results are not yet available
